title: Robust controlled-Z gate for Rydberg atoms based on level-crossing-free echoing rapid adiabatic passage
authors: Yichi Zhang, Zhenqi Bai, Xu Zhao, Hongyan Fan, Ximo Wang, Tiecheng Wang
abstract: We propose a controlled-Z gate scheme for Rydberg atoms based on level-crossing-free echoing rapid adiabatic population transfer. We design antisymmetric Rabi frequency pulses and symmetric detuning pulses, enabling the system to completely avoid level-crossing points throughout the evolution, and the dynamical phase is naturally eliminated by the time-reversal symmetry of the double-pulse sequence. We incorporate dissipative effects through the Lindblad master equation. The numerical simulation yields a two-qubit CZ gate fidelity of 0.9999. When the Rabi-frequency fluctuation is within $\pm 2\%$, and the detuning offset is within $\pm 1\%$, the fidelity can still remain above 0.999. Under the same dissipative model, the three-qubit CCZ gate achieves a fidelity of 0.999. When a single-parameter fluctuation does not exceed $\pm 3\%$, the fidelity is always higher than 0.997. Our scheme requires no laser phase jumps or fast switching operations. The zero-area pulse structure suppresses first-order intensity noise, and the symmetric double-pulse sequence avoids spatially resolved laser switching, making it suitable for parallel gate operations in large-scale neutral-atom arrays.
summary: The paper proposes a novel, robust method to implement controlled-Z gates on Rydberg atoms using level-crossing-free adiabatic passage. By designing specific pulse sequences with zero net area, the scheme naturally cancels unwanted phases and maintains high fidelity ($>0.999$) even when subjected to realistic experimental noise and dissipation. This makes it a highly promising platform for scalable quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to design a highly robust controlled-Z (CZ) gate for Rydberg atoms that minimizes decoherence and remains functional despite experimental imperfections.
main_result: The proposed level-crossing-free echoing rapid adiabatic passage scheme achieves very high fidelity ($0.9999$ for CZ) while being remarkably resilient to laser intensity fluctuations ($\pm 2\%$) and detuning offsets ($\pm 1\%$).
method: The authors employ a double-pulse sequence utilizing antisymmetric Rabi frequency pulses and symmetric detuning pulses, which naturally cancels the dynamical phase via time-reversal symmetry.
model_or_system: The system involves Rydberg atoms in neutral atom arrays, modeled using the Lindblad master equation to account for dissipation. The gate relies on the strong Rydberg blockade effect restricting dynamics to low-excitation subspaces.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), nonadiabatic transition probability ($P_{	ext{nonad}}$), and population evolution during the gate time ($	au_{	ext{gate}}$).
important_parameters: Rabi frequency fluctuation ($\pm 2\%$), detuning offset ($\pm 1\%$), blockade interaction strength ($V_0$), and gate duration ($	au_{	ext{gate}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be effectively described by restricting evolution to low-dimensional subspaces due to the Rydberg blockade, and that the pulse structure ensures zero-area conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic level structures (FIG. 1), pulse profiles for CZ/CCZ gates (FIG. 2(a)), instantaneous eigenenergies showing avoided crossings (FIG. 2(b)), and Bloch sphere trajectories demonstrating controlled phase accumulation.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by comparing adiabatic passage schemes, establishing that level-crossing-free zero-area pulses are superior for robustness. It then applies this framework to simulate CZ/CCZ gates under dissipation using the Lindblad master equation, quantifying fidelity and noise resilience.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant advancement in quantum gate implementation by providing an architecture (level-crossing-free echoing RAP) that intrinsically suppresses common sources of error like laser intensity noise and dynamical phase accumulation, making it highly practical for large arrays.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic of the pulse design and atomic–evel structure. (a)Atomic level structure of two-atom qubits featuring Rydberg–Rydberg interactions between the |r⟩states. (b)Two identical level-crossing-free pulses. The Rabi frequency Ω(t) exhibits an antisymmetric bipolar structure, crossing zero and changing sign at the pulse center; the detuning ∆(t) has a single-peak symmetric structure, smoothly approaching zero at the beginning and end.

FIG. 2: Pulse design and system evolution for CZ and CCZ gates. (a) Profile of the pulses, ∆(t) and Ω(t), for CZ and CCZ gate construction. (b) Instantaneous eigenenergies of the Hamiltonian H(t) during one pulse: the blue and red solid lines represent the eigenstates of the two-atom and single-atom systems, respectively. (c) The atomic population evolution during the complete gate time τgate. The solid line represents the states evolution of the double-atom case, and the dashed line represents the single-atom case. Inset: Bloch sphere trajectory of the dynamical state.

FIG. 3: Fidelity and parameter robustness analysis for CZ and CCZ gates. (a) and (b): Variation of the infidelity with V0 at different total gate times for the CZ and CCZ gates, respectively. (c) and (d): Contour plots of the fidelity for the CZ and CCZ gates against parameter fluctuations, with Ωmax = (2π) 14.93 MHz, ∆0 = 0.45 Ωmax, τR = 11.1, τD = 8.58 for the CZ gate, and Ωmax = (2π) 13.75 MHz, ∆0 = 0.14 Ωmax, τR = 12, τD = 9.15 for the CCZ gate. The total gate time is 3.92 µs for both gates.
